# Tino Rabe

> Freelance Dynamics 365 CRM & Power Platform consultant and Power Pages specialist, based in Laboe near Kiel, Germany. Opens Dynamics 365 securely to customers and partners: customer portals, partner portals and self-service on Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service and Field Service. Former Microsoft MVP for Power Pages (2024 to 2026). Works remotely for clients and Microsoft partners in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Site languages: German and English. Home and service pages exist in both languages (English under /en/); most articles in both.

Grown with Dynamics 365 and Power Platform. Known for Power Pages. Delivering across the whole platform.

## About

- Working with Dynamics CRM and portals since 2014, starting with Adxstudio portals at Avanade; later ascendit, proMX and adesso; freelance since 2025.
- Followed the portal product through every rename: Adxstudio, Dynamics 365 Portals, Power Apps Portals, Power Pages.
- Microsoft exams on Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Engagement, Power Platform and Field Service (2018 to 2021).
- Talks 2024 to 2026, including Days of Knowledge (Odense), Collabdays Hamburg and the Global Power Platform Bootcamp.
- Education: IT systems management assistant (IT-Systemkaufmann), Bachelor of Arts in Business Informatics (FH Kiel).
- About page: https://tinorabe.de/en/about/ (DE: https://tinorabe.de/ueber-mich/)

## Services

1. **Delivery: Dynamics 365 CRM & Power Platform** (build right): solution architecture, delivery or review for Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service and Field Service, Dataverse, model-driven apps, Power Automate and Power Pages, inside the client's team or the team of their Microsoft partner. Data model, internal security roles and external permissions are planned together from the start.
   https://tinorabe.de/en/services/dynamics-365-crm/ (DE: https://tinorabe.de/leistungen/dynamics-365-crm/)
2. **Security audit for Power Pages** (prove it's right): independent, strictly read-only remote review of a live portal on Dynamics 365 in eight areas, including table permissions, Web API column exposure, authentication and configuration. Report with findings rated by severity and concrete measures. About two weeks. Fixed price EUR 4,900 net, EUR 6,900 net for high complexity.
   https://tinorabe.de/en/services/security-audit/ (DE: https://tinorabe.de/leistungen/security-audit/)
3. **Care for portals on Dynamics 365** (keep it right): monthly security and configuration review, Microsoft release check with assessment, written monthly report, small changes included. Care EUR 1,290 net per month, Care Plus EUR 2,490 net per month, minimum term three months.
   https://tinorabe.de/en/services/care/ (DE: https://tinorabe.de/leistungen/care/)

All prices are net, plus VAT.

- [32 MB Passes, 4 MB Fails: What the Power Pages Server Logic Memory Limit Actually Does](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-server-logic-memory-limit/): Measured behavior of the undocumented Server Logic memory limit: periodic check, what fits, what logging does, what MaxMemoryUsageInBytes changes, and a budget for your data (English only)
- [In-House or Specialist for Your Power Pages Portal? An Honest Take](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-in-house-vs-specialist/): When your own team should run a Power Pages portal, when a specialist makes sense, and why splitting the job (team for daily changes, specialist for monthly security, update and configuration reviews) is often the best answer. (English only)
- [Internal Tools on Dynamics 365: Check the License Context Before You Build](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/d365-power-pages-internal-users/): Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses include internal Power Pages sites and Power Apps use rights, but only within the licensed application context and environment. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/d365-power-pages-internal-users/)
- [New HTML Features in 2026: What's Actually Ready for Power Pages Today](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-html-2026-features/): Which 2026 HTML features (base-select, popover, invoker commands, hidden until-found, sizes auto) are actually Baseline for a Power Pages browser mix with Firefox and Safari, plus a shipped portal CSS reset that silently breaks hidden="until-found". (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-html-2026-features/)
- [Power Pages Terms & Conditions: The Complete Setup (and the Silent Failure Everyone Hits)](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-terms-conditions/): Complete Terms & Conditions setup in Power Pages. One documented site setting plus the TermsAndConditionsCopy content snippet that is empty by default and silently breaks the whole dialog when left empty; plus the sign-in-only trigger that makes it invisible to already-logged-in test users. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-terms-conditions/)
- [Fetching N:M data on demand with Power Pages Server Logic](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-server-logic-nm-ondemand/): The follow-up to the Web API N:M post: Server Logic reads a many-to-many relationship server-side via $expand (verified live, HTTP 200) through Server.Connector.Dataverse, the on-demand alternative to preloaded Liquid FetchXML, plus the permission-bound-but-not-safe authorization caveat and the timeout/no-fetch limits. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-server-logic-nm-ondemand/)
- [Calling Server Logic from Liquid: the full circle in Power Pages](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-serverlogic-from-liquid/): Trilogy capstone. The serverlogic Liquid tag runs a reusable server-side operation at page render, no client call and no CSRF token, rendering the N:M list from part one via the Server.Connector.Dataverse operation from part two (verified live). Includes the connector {StatusCode,Body} envelope gotcha, the compiled-logic caching gotcha, and Server.Context.Input vs QueryParameters (one function, two contexts). (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-serverlogic-from-liquid/)
- [Bulk-Managing Power Pages Content Snippets: The Excel Round-Trip](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-content-snippet-bulk-import/): Bulk-manage Power Pages content snippets via the enhanced data model's Site Component (powerpagecomponent) table and the Dataverse Export/Edit-in-Excel round-trip, including the JSON Content column and its observed envelope format and the pitfalls of the hidden control columns. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-content-snippet-bulk-import/)
- [Reading N:M relationships in Power Pages: Web API vs. Liquid FetchXML](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-webapi-nm-relationships/): The portal Web API can't conveniently read many-to-many relationships (documented Known Issue with multi-level permissions and Contact/Account scopes); Microsoft's own workaround is Liquid FetchXML via link-entity/intersect, proven live, with the permission/auth trap that makes results silently empty. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-webapi-nm-relationships/)
- [End-to-End Value: Why Portal ≠ Nice-to-Have (It's Essential)](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/d365-portal-business-case/): Power Pages licenses per website, not per Dynamics 365 workload, so one portal can cover Customer Service, Sales, and Field Service under a single user pool. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/d365-portal-business-case/)
- [Power Pages Server Logic: 4 Hidden Constraints That Will Break Your Code](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-server-logic-hidden-constraints/): The documented blocklist versus four undocumented constraints in Server Logic found by live bisection testing, plus a debugging playbook. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-server-logic-versteckte-grenzen/)
- [Beyond Internal Silos: Extending Dynamics 365 to Partners and Suppliers](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/d365-partner-ecosystem/): The Dynamics 365 Partner Relationship Management template gives resellers and suppliers real-time, role-scoped access without a D365 seat. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/d365-partner-ecosystem/)
- [Power Pages Security Selfcheck: 5 Checks, 15 Minutes](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/security-selfcheck/): Five free Power Pages security checks you can run in fifteen minutes, no tools or budget required: anonymous API access, Site Checker, table permissions, and more. (English only)
- [The Render-Mutate-Refresh Pattern: Liquid + Server Logic in Power Pages](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-render-mutate-refresh-pattern/): An architecture pattern combining server-rendered Liquid, Server Logic writes and explicit resync for data-bound, user-specific Power Pages components, with its permission-scope trade-offs. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-render-mutate-refresh-muster/)
- [The 75-25 Dilemma: Why Your Dynamics 365 Investment Stops at Your Door](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/d365-75-25-dilemma/): Dynamics 365 covers internal work well; external access for customers and partners needs its own Power Pages license and a portal. - [It Wasn't a Hack. Your Power Pages Config Was.](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/wasnt-a-hack/): The Power Pages data leaks that hit over a dozen organizations and millions of records happened without a single exploit; the misconfiguration pattern behind them (anonymous web role, table permissions) and what to audit. What operators should learn, with a timeline. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/haertungs-serie-2026/)
- [OData Filter Eats Your # Character: A Dataverse Web API Gotcha](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/dataverse-odata-filter-hash-character/): Why an unescaped # in an OData $filter value gets stripped before the request is sent, when it fails loudly versus silently, and the correct escaping order. (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/dataverse-odata-filter-rautezeichen/)
- [The Power Pages Wildcard Fix Has One Documented Exception](https://tinorabe.de/en/blog/power-pages-wildcard-fix-richtextfile-exception/): Microsoft's own rich text editor tutorial still recommends the wildcard value for msdyn_richtextfile; why that is a documented exception, and the full field list to fix it correctly (DE: https://tinorabe.de/de/blog/power-pages-wildcard-fix-richtextfile-exception/)

(English only)

(English only)
